newsitem.title: USA: New York man arrested in Mexican slave-labor case.
newsitem.headline: New York man arrested in Mexican slave-labor case.

text.p: Police arrested a 37-year-old man in connection with claims by dozens of deaf Mexicans, rescued by authorities on Saturday, who said they were forced to work for him for slave wages in New York.

The case came to light when four deaf-mute Mexican men walked into the police station in Jackson Heights, in the New York City borough of Queens, at 5 a.m. EDT (0900 GMT). In sign language, they told a bizarre story of being held captive along with dozens of other deaf Mexicans, by a man who forced them to work selling trinkets on the streets for slave wages.
Police went to the two locations described by the four men, and rescued 58 other men, women and children. It was not clear how long the Mexicans had been captive, police said.

Forty-four people were found at the first location and 18 at the second site. Police said the Mexicans were living in two-family attached homes that could only house seven or eight people. "They were living on mattresses on the floor," police said.
Police identified the man who was arrested and was being questioned as Alfred Paoletti or Alfredo Rustrian.

"It appears that there was one man and possibly more holding a number of people in bondage and virtual slavery," New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said at a news conference. "This is a very disgusting and horrible situation."
Of the 62 Mexicans rescued by police, 30 were women and 10 were children. The mayor indicated there may be more Mexicans being held at other locations.

Giuliani said it was alleged that the man being questioned forced the Mexicans to work for him and then took their wages from them. "All of these people were deaf mutes so in addition to taking these people into bondage and requiring that they work for him, he was also taking advantage of people with disabilities," he said.
The mayor also said "it is being alleged that the man physically and sexually abused" the Mexicans.
"All of the adults and children seemed to be in good health," police spokesman Arek Tarih said. "The children only speak Spanish."

The deaf-mute Mexicans told police in sign language that they were brought here from Mexico and were made to work the streets of Manhattan, Queens and New Jersey peddling trinkets such as key chains, pens and toys.
"We are still trying to sort out what transpired. It is not clear where in Mexico these people were recruited and who brought them here," Tarih said.

Police communicated with the deaf mutes through sign language interpreters. "They are telling us they are legal immigrants but that their documents were taken away from them by the person who brought them to the United States," he added.
